title: Powassan virus encephalitis CSF metagenomic reads
study_ids: Piantadosi et al. 2018, Rapid Detection of Powassan Virus in a Patient With Encephalitis by Metagenomic Sequencing; DOI 10.1093/cid/cix792

provenance.description: Clinical metagenomic reads from cerebrospinal fluid; tutorial says 14 million short nucleotide reads were produced and human reads were removed with Kraken, leaving 226,908 reads. The tutorial provides a processed FASTA mystery_reads.fasta. The exact underlying SRA accession is not stated in the inspected tutorial and remains unknown.

biological_context.experimental_units: One encephalitis patient; CSF; tutorial says sequencing was performed on hospital day 8. Paper reports multiple sample types and sequencing runs, so mapping this tutorial FASTA to a specific library/run is unresolved.
biological_context.assay: Metagenomic sequencing of short nucleotide reads
biological_context.design: Clinical case investigation; control and library context are not specified for the particular tutorial FASTA.

assets.processing_stage: Tutorial-provided reads after Kraken removal of human reads; paired-end merging with FLASH is described nearby but whether this FASTA reflects that merge is unresolved.
assets.relationship: Derived tutorial input; exact SRA source accession and processing history are not supplied.

access_and_terms.access_requirements: Public HTTP download URL in tutorial; current availability not checked.
access_and_terms.redistribution: Unknown; public URL does not establish redistribution eligibility.

inspection.checked: Tutorial prose identifying the clinical specimen, read counts, Kraken human-read filtering, and URL for mystery_reads.fasta; PubMed Central paper search result corroborates clinical Powassan virus case and sequencing context.
unverified: SRA accession, exact linkage between FASTA and paper sample/run, file size/hash, file contents, permissions, and whether tutorial's count is current or per-run.

limitations: Do not infer the missing SRA accession from the paper title. The tutorial file is the actionable identified input, but its lineage to the source run needs verification.
Tutorial reports 14 million reads and 226,908 retained reads; these counts were copied from documentation, not reproduced by inspection of the data.

title: Saccharomyces cerevisiae S288C chromosome I segment used in contig-taxonomy tutorial

provenance.description: Tutorial retrieves a sequence segment from the pinned soedinglab/metaeuk-regression repository. FASTA header identifies Saccharomyces cerevisiae S288C chromosome I, complete sequence; accession coordinate suffix identifies segment 100425-153163.

biological_context.experimental_units: Reference genomic sequence segment, not a biological sample

assets.processing_stage: Extracted chromosome segment supplied as the contig input in a taxonomy tutorial
assets.relationship: Companion sacc_prots_in_segment.fa contains 19 annotated proteins coded on the contig; tutorial says those proteins are not used in the assignment.

assets.processing_stage: Companion annotated proteins for comparison only; not consumed by tutorial workflow
assets.relationship: Proteins coded on the reference segment; tutorial states 19 proteins.

access_and_terms.redistribution: Unknown for the source asset; inspect upstream repository license before reuse.

inspection.checked: Pinned repository FASTA, including bounded header and sequence preview; tutorial statement about the unconsumed annotated protein companion.
unverified: File size/hash, segment sequence length, upstream license terms, and identity of the Swiss-Prot database release used by the tutorial.

limitations: This is a reference-genome segment fixture, not a clinical or environmental observation.
Swiss-Prot reference input is dynamic and unversioned in the tutorial; no exact reference release is associated with the assignment.
